$comment: v2.3 plan 03. Every place in src/runtime, src/wizard, src/extraction and src/generation (V3) that writes AFTER an await — methods, function declarations, and since V3 arrow functions (named by where they live) and property assignments, and what has been done about it. Generated set, hand-classified status. The guard in src/runtime/ownership.guard.test.ts fails when this file and the code disagree, in EITHER direction: a new site nobody classified, a row whose site is gone, a "checked" row with no token check in its body, or a "todo" row that has quietly acquired one (flip it to checked). Statuses: checked (verifies a RunToken before writing) | delegate (awaits a censused site that owns the check) | local (writes nothing that outlives the call) | todo (owed work). WHAT "checked" MEANS, PRECISELY: the body contains a token check -- NOT that every write is preceded by one. The detector is a body-level scan, so it cannot see the interleaving, and a body that gains a fifth host step can escape the checks that guard the other four (found 2026-09-22 in EffectsApplier.applyCheckpoint: the preset sat below the Author Note await and the background below applyCastChanges per-member awaits). Per-write checking is proven by TESTS in the case files (effectsOwnership.review.test.ts pins each check with a case that reaches it), which is also the file-level rule: a check without a case is a check a mutation can delete.

src/runtime/spikes/swipeBack.ts#SwipeBac.note: v2.5 plan 09 SP1 spike (2026-09-26; dev-only import, install-wide flag spikes.swipeBackCache, default off): the run minted when the bridge handed the swipe over is checked before the record is written back. loadSelectedFromChat starts a new epoch by design, so after it the chat id and the engine's last message are compared with the cache key before the queued writes are re-enqueued, and a run minted after the load is checked before notify. persist goes through the ChatSave chokepoint, which refuses another chat's write; the stats it bumps are in-memory counters.

src/runtime/spikes/recommitEdit.ts#Recom.note: v2.5 plan 09 SP2 spike (2026-09-26; dev-only import, install-wide flag spikes.recommitEdit, default off): the run is minted when the bridge hands the edit over, before the rollback, and is re-checked on entry, after the rollback (before the re-enqueue and the re-commit) and after the re-commit (before the read). commitBoundary and runExtractionNow mint their own runs; the stats it bumps are in-memory counters.

src/runtime/wiring/spikes.ts#refreshSpik.note: v2.5 plan 09 SP9 spike (2026-09-26): after awaiting the dev-only import of the witness filter it writes only the module-level spikeHooks.witness slot and its own dispose handle, in memory, and only while its own epoch is current (a later refresh or stopSpikes bumps it). Nothing chat-scoped or persisted; the filter it starts keeps its witness records in WeakMaps keyed by live message objects and never writes the chat.

src/runtime/promptCost.ts#PromptCost.flu.note: v2.4 plan 08 T19a (2026-09-25): writes only the cache's own in-memory count map (tokens per block hash) and calls notify; nothing is persisted or chat-scoped, and a detach mid-flush stops the write (host identity check). src/extraction/scheduler.ts#ExtractionSc.note: v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): COVERED: the read's guard is minted before runSharedRead and travels into applyExtractionAudit, which refuses a lapsed read before any write (V2); the panel's lastError is written only when the epoch the job started in is still current (sameWorld). NOT COVERED: `inFlight` is one flag per scheduler, so a new world's queue waits for an old job to finish (serial by design: one endpoint), and `job.run` bodies are censused where they are defined, not here. v2.4 plan 03 D2 (2026-09-24): the read's guard now carries a live signal into the model call, so a mutation inside its window or a new world ABORTS the host request (runOwner.abort.test.ts); a lapse is not retried, writes no lastError and never reaches the pause path (scheduler.test.ts "an aborted read is not retried and records no error"); an in-flight answer that wins the race against the abort is still refused at the write edge. v2.4 plan 03 D3 (2026-09-24): the install-wide pause is DELETED (no src module writes extraction.enabled, extractionEnabled.guard.test.ts). A failure is classified: transport/timeout opens the in-memory, per-profile breaker and re-queues the job only while the job's epoch is current (a switched-away job is dropped, never carried into the new world); config sets the install-level config problem (not per chat, so not epoch-guarded) and drops the job; a bug (non-ModelCallError) writes the sameWorld-guarded lastError and a journal line, cleared at the next boundary. Cases: scheduler.breaker.test.ts. Live-found fix (2026-09-24, D2): a read whose guard lapsed on a WINDOW mutation (thrown lapse, or refused at the write edge) holds the light queue until the mutation's rollback settles (bounded at 10 s), then re-queues a P0 reread:lapsed over its window re-clamped to the chat, only while the job's epoch is still current; it merges into an overlapping queued rollback re-read. The re-queue writes scheduler state only (in memory). Cases: schedulerReread.review.test.ts. v2.4 plan 08 T18 (2026-09-25): a transport failure trips the breaker of the profile the call actually went to (ModelCallError.profileId), and the job is re-queued held on that id; the queue skips a job whose own breaker is open, so a dead routed profile holds only its own passes. Cases: scheduler.routes.test.ts.

v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): COVERED: lastHeavyError is written only when the job's starting epoch is still current (it used to land in the next world's panel after clearForNewWorld emptied it). NOT COVERED: heavyInFlight serialises across worlds by design, and the job's own writes live in its run closure, censused at its definition. v2.4 plan 03 D2 (2026-09-24): a lapsed heavy job (aborted by the epoch) is not retried and writes no lastHeavyError. v2.4 plan 03 D3 (2026-09-24): heavy jobs share the breaker. A transport failure opens it and re-queues the heavy job only in its own epoch; lastHeavyError is kept for bug-class failures (sameWorld-guarded); a config failure sets the config problem. v2.4 plan 08 T18 (2026-09-25): same per-profile hold as pump; a dead curator profile holds only the curator's heavy job (scheduler.routes.test.ts).

v2.4 plan 03 D3 (2026-09-24): the breaker's half-open probe. After awaiting the PONG probe it writes only scheduler-owned in-memory state (the breaker entry, the install-level config problem, the probe timer) and re-pumps; nothing is chat state or persisted, and it re-checks that the breaker is still open for that profile before writing, so a profile deleted meanwhile is not re-opened. RuntimeManager.retryExtraction (Try again) is a one-line delegate that writes nothing, so the census has no row for it. v2.4 plan 08 T18 (2026-09-25): probes run per profile id (one timer and one in-flight probe per id); a config answer on the read profile sets the install-level config problem, on any other routed profile it sets that profile's own problem (profileProblems), in memory only. v2.4 acceptance A6 (2026-09-25): the probe's budget is read BEFORE the await (probeTimeoutMs over the entry's step and the slowest answered call), so no new write follows it. Its sibling ExtractionScheduler.noteAnswered is synchronous (called from the client's answered observer after the reply resolved) and so is no census site.

v2.3 plan 11 §Fault matrix: found by the census, not by a journey. The model call runs for minutes and every write below it resolved to whichever chat was open when it answered, so a chain generated for chat A was filed into chat B's cache and merged into chat B's story — the last async coordinator without a token. Checked after the generation and again in the catch and before the persist, because the failure path is a write too. The `generating` marker written before the await still stays in chat A after a switch, but since v2.4 plan 03 D4 it no longer blocks its key: the in-memory live-job map (a RunGuard per key, released in `finally`) is what queue() consults, and a marker no live job of this world holds is re-queued on return; hydrate demotes a persisted queued/generating entry (sanitizeExpansion). The `finally` release is in-memory only (local). v2.4 plan 03 D3 (2026-09-24): a transport failure is rethrown only after the failed marker, persist and notify, all behind the same run check, so the scheduler's breaker can count it; a switched-away run returns before any of that (abortedCall.review.test.ts).

src/runtime/coordinators/extractionCoord.note: v2.3 plan 03: the main extraction write path. verifyEntries is a judge pass, and everything after it deposits the read conclusions into the memory tiers, the epistemic and ledger stores and the audit ring. Minted with the audit window: these entries are claims ABOUT the messages read, so an edit inside that span invalidates them while a reply appended after it does not. Re-checked after every awaited stage (verify, applyEntries, save) rather than once, because a single check on the near side of an await is what C1 was. RESIDUAL: enqueueExtractorDeltas runs before the await and is not covered.

v2.3 plan 03: TWO model calls with a store written in between, so the check sits after each call rather than once at the end — the epistemic signals are applied before the ledger prompt is even sent. Both stores and the injection update are refused when the world moved.

src/runtime/memorizeBacklog.ts#MemorizeB.note: v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): mints one read over the whole chat before the first await, asks it before every window, passes it into applyAudit (which refuses a lapsed read before any write), and asks again before the final read, the boundary commit and the error record. It used to read the NEXT chat's windows into memory after a switch. v2.4 plan 03 D4 (2026-09-24): the loop moved to memorizeWindows and the exit to endBacklog, so every ending passes through one write. The read it hands on is the chat token AND the backlog's own Stop controller (cancelMemorizeBacklog), checked between windows. Its only write after the await is clearing its own in-memory `backlogStop` handle. v2.4 plan 03 D5 wiring (2026-09-24): the read is minted BEFORE the plan's token count (an await), and the preflight popup is another await before anything is sent; the plan is refused when the read lapsed during either. The model calls now carry anySignal([Stop, read.signal]), so Stop and a mutation inside the whole-chat window cancel the request in flight (budgetWiring.review.test.ts).

v2.4 plan 03 D4 (2026-09-24): the backlog's one exit. Reads read.lapsed() BEFORE its only write: an epoch/chat/story lapse writes nothing (the backfill it would clear belongs to another chat, whose hydrate resets running itself); a same-chat lapse (window: an edit or swipe inside the whole-chat read; version: a hot-swapped story) and a player Stop write running:false with a reason. This is what closes the same-chat wedge, where every early return left running:true until reload.

v2.4 plan 03 D4 (2026-09-24): the V3 window loop, moved out of runMemorizeBacklog unchanged. The ReadOwnership it is handed combines the whole-chat token with the Stop controller, and it is asked before every window, after every applyAudit (which refuses a lapsed read before any write), before the final read and before the boundary commit. A stopped run therefore writes nothing further, and the windows already applied stay (memory-only, acceptedDeltas: []). Live-found fix (2026-09-24): the scene passes a window's audit triggers are collected, not scheduled, and run one at a time after that window (runSceneWork, asked before each pass); each pass keeps its own guard and is censused where it is defined. v2.4 acceptance A11 (2026-09-25): each window read and the whole-chat read go through retryOnTimeout, one more ask at twice the budget after a timeout. The retry is another await INSIDE the read, before the same applyAudit and stillOwns checks, so no write moved past a check; a Stop or chat switch during the first ask is a lapse, which is never retried.

src/runtime/coordinators/stagecraftCoord.note: AE-01 (2026-09-25; was the body of `applyAccepted`, which is now a synchronous wrapper that mints the RunGuard at call time and serializes applies, so two overlapping applies cannot both read one op as accepted and write it twice). These ops reach a real lorebook FILE shared by every chat using the book. The guard is threaded into `writeOp`, which checks it after each of its own awaits; a lapse there returns before any further write and this loop returns without patching. The proposal patch is checked once more after the last op, and it merges the touched records by id into the CURRENT list instead of replacing the list with the snapshot taken at the start. Before AE-01 the only in-loop check sat before the `writeOp` call, so both awaits inside it were unguarded.

src/runtime/curatorWriter.ts#CuratorWrit.note: AE-01 (2026-09-25): was `partial` on "its caller checks the token before every call", the census blind spot, since that check preceded both awaits in here. The RunGuard is now threaded in and checked immediately after the write-edge read (before `beforeHostWrite`, the write-ahead record) and immediately after the write-ahead save (before `updateWIEntryByUid`, its one host write). A lapse returns `lapsed` and records nothing: after a switch, state and save both resolve to the chat that replaced this one. A lapse after the write-ahead save leaves the departed chat's op `accepted` with its pending marker, the same row a crash before the host call leaves; nothing reconciles that marker on hydrate, and the op's next boundary in its own chat re-reads the entry and writes it (stagecraftCoordinator.test.ts, AE-01 block).

src/runtime/effectHost.ts#restoreEffectT.note: PARTIAL: one inverse per effect target, and the GUARD IS THE CALLER. `EffectsApplier.restoreEffects` reads each target's current value and compares it with what this chat wrote before calling anything here, and refuses the ones that no longer hold it — so a restore that outlived its chat cannot overwrite an edit someone else made. The token would add the chat-switch case, which the leave/rollback/restart callers own; each branch here is a single stHost seam whose own result is returned as the answer.
